This application has been prepared as a retrospective Listed Building Consent for the addition of three rooflights in the pitched roofs at the rear of 10 Malvern Terrace. The building is a Grade II Listed Building of architectural and historic interest and is in the Barnsbury Conservation Area. It is a single residential, double-fronted, terraced villa, situated on the north side of Malvern Terrace. The house was previously extended under approved planning application number P112110 and approved listed building consent P112150 (both approved on 07 November 2011), as well as an 'Approval of Details pursuant to Condition 9 of Listed Building Consent application reference P112150 (P112150(C9) – approved on 08 June 2012). In the processing of a later unrelated (and refused) planning application on the site, it has come to light that there are 3no. rooflights in the pitched roof of the extension which were not previously captured in the Listed Building Consent and subsequent Approval of Conditions referenced above. Correspondence with Islington Planning Department dated 10 July 2013 states that the rooflights are not considered harmful and that no further action was considered expedient. Further correspondence dated 23 October 2025 advises that, although the skylights do not appear harmful, formal Listed Building Consent is required as the skylights currently do not have formal consent. It has been established in correspondence with Islington Planning Department, that the rooflights are not considered harmful and that no further action will be taken. However, in response to the planning officer’s advice, this listed building consent is being submitted to gain formal consent for the 3no. rooflights as constructed.
